sections.title: Serverless and messaging

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: Lambda and the messaging services appear in many Java job descriptions, usually for event processing.

blocks.title: An SQS-triggered handler

rows: The JVM and Spring start slowly. Use SnapStart, keep dependencies few, avoid full Spring where you can
Not for long jobs: use ECS tasks or Step Functions
Scales fast and can overwhelm a database: set reserved concurrency, use RDS Proxy
By duration and memory; memory also increases CPU
Spiky, event-driven, short tasks; low traffic
Steady traffic, long requests, existing Spring services

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: SQS may deliver a message twice, and the visibility timeout must exceed processing time, or it is redelivered while still being processed. Make consumers idempotent and configure a dead-letter queue.

sections.title: DynamoDB in one minute
blocks: You design the table from your **access patterns**, not from entities. Items are found by partition key and optional sort key; other queries need a secondary index or a scan, which is slow and expensive. A bad partition key creates a hot partition. Choose it for strongly known, key-based access at huge scale. If you need flexible queries and joins, stay with PostgreSQL.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Handlers must be idempotent, and report partial batch failures.
- Use SnapStart and few dependencies for Java cold starts.
- Protect the database from Lambda concurrency.
- Kafka-like replay needs MSK or Kinesis, not SQS.

items.question: Why might you not run your Spring Boot API on Lambda?
items.answer: Cold starts, per-instance connection handling and long-lived behaviour fit containers better when traffic is steady.

items.question: Messages are processed twice during a slow period. Why?
items.answer: Processing exceeded the visibility timeout, so SQS redelivered. Increase the timeout, and make processing idempotent anyway.
